intro: This last unit asks two things. First, it looks at the Qur'an as sound and sight: the doctrine that no one can imitate it, the reciters whose voices fill stadiums and radio stations, the calligraphers who shaped its letters, and the mosques whose walls carry its words. Muslims have read the book with their ears and eyes as much as with their minds.

Then it hands the work to you. In the capstone you choose one verse or a short surah and one question. You read it in two translations, place it in its surah and its history, and gather what classical and modern commentators have said. Then you write and present your own careful argument about what the verse says and how it has been read.

By the end you will be able to explain i'jaz, recitation styles and the main calligraphic scripts. You will also be able to cite surah and ayah, translator and commentator, and describe readings you do not hold fairly. Those are the skills of anyone who studies a text people care about deeply.
bigQuestion: How have people experienced the Qur'an through sound, art and careful reading, and how can a student describe those readings fairly?

timeline.t: Muslim tradition dates the first revelation to Muhammad near Mecca
Al-Tabari, author of a vast commentary, dies in Baghdad
Ibn al-Bawwab copies a Qur'an in rounded scripts in Baghdad
Al-Wahidi, compiler of the occasions of revelation, dies
Fakhr al-Din al-Razi, the philosopher-commentator, dies
Ibn Kathir, whose commentary is still widely read, dies
The Cairo edition of the Qur'an is printed and becomes a standard
Marmaduke Pickthall publishes The Meaning of the Glorious Koran
Abington v. Schempp: U.S. schools may teach about religion
Tabataba'i, author of the Shia commentary al-Mizan, dies
Abdul Basit Abdus Samad, the famed Egyptian reciter, dies

test.q: What does the doctrine of i'jaz hold?
choices: The Qur'an must be recited in a group
The Qur'an was written in Kufic first
The Qur'an may not be translated
test.why: I'jaz is inimitability, rooted in the challenge verses such as 17:88.

test.q: Which verse dares humans and jinn together to produce the like of the Qur'an?
test.why: Surah 17 (Al-Isra), ayah 88, is a challenge verse.

choices: The rules for reciting the Qur'an with correct sound
test.why: Tajwid governs pronunciation, length and rhythm in recitation.

test.q: How does mujawwad recitation differ from murattal?
choices: It is silent and read only by eye
It is slower and more melodic, for listeners
It uses a different Arabic text
It is only used in Shia mosques
test.why: Murattal is measured and steady; mujawwad is slow and ornamented.

test.q: Which script is angular and found in many early Qur'ans?
test.why: Kufic is the early angular script; Naskh and Thuluth are rounded.

test.q: Which short surah is often inscribed on buildings and speaks of God as One?
test.why: Al-Ikhlas (112) states God's oneness in four ayat.

test.q: Why does the capstone ask for at least one public-domain translation?
choices: So the student can quote it exactly
Because only old translations are Muslim
Because public schools forbid new books
test.why: Public-domain texts like Pickthall (1930) may be quoted; modern ones are described.
Siyaq is the context in the text.

choices: The thirty parts of the Qur'an
Reports of the events that prompted verses
test.why: They are the occasions of revelation, compiled by scholars such as al-Wahidi.

test.q: Which commentator died in 923 and gathered earlier reports on each verse?
test.why: Al-Tabari's Jami' al-Bayan collects the views of earlier generations.

test.q: What does it mean to explain the Qur'an by the Qur'an?
choices: Reciting the whole book in one night
Reading one verse in light of other verses
test.why: This classical method is praised by Ibn Taymiyya and used by Ibn Kathir.

test.q: Which is a good capstone thesis?
choices: The Qur'an is the most beautiful book
Classical and modern commentators read 2:256 differently, for reasons tied to its context
test.why: A thesis makes a checkable claim about the text and its readers.

test.q: What did Abington v. Schempp (1963) allow public schools to do?
test.why: The Court ended devotional exercises but affirmed academic study of religion.

test.q: How should an essay treat a reading it does not follow?
choices: Describe it fairly, in words its holders would accept
Call it wrong without a reason
Replace it with the student's belief
test.why: Charitable, attributed description is the heart of the course.

write.prompt: Choose one verse or short surah studied in this unit (for example 2:256, 17:88 or Surah 112). Pose a question about it, cite the verse in two translations and at least two commentators, and explain what the text says and how its readers have read it.
tips: Name the surah, ayah, translator and year every time you quote.
Attribute every reading: al-Tabari reports, Muslims believe, historians note.
Describe readings you do not follow fairly before giving your thesis.
Compare readers rather than judge the text.
Use the unit's terms, such as siyaq, tafsir and asbab al-nuzul.
